text:
maria: FYI our client harness numbers look fine, but replaying live traffic we see p99 spikes and lower throughput. I think keepalive + TLS + Nagle interactions are masking perf in the synthetic tests.

sam: Can you paste the harness config? Are you using separate connections per request or a pooled client?

maria: Pooled, but the pool size was tiny (10) and we were opening new TLS sessions often. Replay uses long-lived connections.

jin: That alone can flip kernel scheduling behaviour. Short-lived connections -> lots of accept()/close() syscalls which change CPU steal and epoll churn.

kevin: Also watch TCP_NODELAY. Default Nagle can coalesce small writes into larger TLS records, which changes write syscall patterns and triggers different kernel path/kernels in our runtime.

maria: Repro steps I used:
```
# client harness baseline
wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --latency http://localhost:8080/api/generate
# replay harness (pcap converted)
python replay_harness.py --capture live.pcap --rate 1x
```
The wrk run looks fine, replay shows tails.

sam: Two quick hypotheses: 1) TLS handshake cost and session resumption different; 2) KV cache warmup is misaligned — replay hits hot prefixes which cause larger batches and different kernel selection.

jin: Agree. Our runtime picks different GEMM kernels when sequence length distribution or batch shape changes. If replay causes many short sequences to hit the KV cache, the runtime may switch to the small-seq execution path which has higher fixed overhead per request.

kevin: We should make the harnesses apples-to-apples: same connection lifetime, same TLS session reuse (tickets), same number of concurrent streams (HTTP/2), identical request batching windows.

maria: Also saw from perf script: spikes in context-switches and tcp:prune_timer events when the harness used many short TCP conns. Kernel scheduling looked different across cores.

sam: Can you add perf + tracepoint for tcp and sched while replaying? Something like:
```
sudo perf record -e sched:sched_switch -e tcp:tcp_rcv_space_adjust -a -o perf.data -- sleep 60
sudo perf script | head -n200
```
That should surface epoll vs accept churn.

jin: For gRPC vs REST note: grpc (http2) multiplexes on one connection so it hides TLS handshake cost but may exhibit head-of-line blocking on a connection with big token returns. REST (http1.1) with keepalive+pipelining (or multiple connections) shows different per-connection syscalls. They are not comparable unless you control for connection reuse and concurrency.

kevin: TLDR checklist for apples-to-apples:
- Same connection lifetime and reuse semantics (reuse TLS sessions or disable session tickets consistent across tests)
- Same TCP_NODELAY setting
- Same client-side connection count and per-conn concurrency
- Pre-warm KV cache with representative prefixes before measurement
- Use identical sequence length distribution or replay with scaled timestamps
- Collect kernel traces and runtime traces for a subset runs

maria: I added a small harness patch to enforce TCP_NODELAY and session reuse for wrk-based runs. Also added a pre-warm step:
```
# pre-warm kv cache
python bulk_warm.py --prompts warm_prompts.json --concurrency 50 --rate 200/s
```
After pre-warm, replay p99 improved ~15% but still off by ~7%.

sam: That remaining delta could be due to TLS record sizes. If client aggregates smaller application writes into fewer TLS records, the runtime sees larger recv() slices and different deserialization batching. Try forcing 1 write per message vs batching at client.

jin: Also check socket recv buffer sizes. rcvbuf influences coalescing. Kernel may switch assembly kernels if it sees larger contiguous buffers.

kevin: For regression hunting — isolate: 1) synthetic wrk with forced long-lived TLS sessions + TCP_NODELAY + pre-warm; 2) same as (1) but with replayed timing; 3) compare perf maps and kernel selection logs from runtime (enable --dump-kernel-decisions).

maria: I'll run the three variants now and push profiles to the perf bucket.

deploy-bot: Reminder: load-test cluster has a quota. Please tag runs with `bench/redwood/kv-warm` and notify ops if >1hr.

sam: One more note: when measuring tokens/sec don't forget to separate client-side serialization CPU from server-side GPU time. Use nvidia-smi sampling and top -H on the server to split CPU pain.

jin: Good point. Also capture TLS CPU with 'sslsnoop' or count openssl handles. Session resumption (tickets) reduces CPU and latency.

maria: Ok action items: I'll run the controlled suite, capture perf+tcp traces, and upload kernel decision dumps. Jin will correlate kernel choices with sequence shape. Sam will craft an apples-to-apples benchmark matrix. Kevin will look at Nagle/rcvbuf heuristics in the client lib.

kevin: If we find a stable difference linked to client behavior we should add a 'client-compatibility' section to the benchmark docs describing exact socket/TLS settings to reproduce production.

maria: sounds good. Thanks all.

jin: ping me when you upload perf data, I'll start the kernel-decisions diff.
